Anderson, Born 08/02/1993 in California |url=https://californiabirthindex.org/birth/gabriel_russell_anderson_born_1993_21940383 |website=CaliforniaBirthIndex.org |access-date=15 August 2024}} (born August 2, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]], earning second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] as a senior in 2015–16. ==High school career== York attended [[Lutheran High School of Orange County|Orange Lutheran High School]] in [[Orange, California]]. He averaged 24.9 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 2.3 steals per game as a senior where he became the all-time leading scorer of the school. He was rated as the No. 46 overall prospect and No. 11 [[shooting guard]] in the class of 2012 by [[Rivals.com]] and a scout grade of 93 by [[ESPN]]. He signed to Arizona on July 10, 2011.{{cite web | url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207988083 | title= Gabe York Biography | work=ArizonaWildcats.com | accessdate=December 19, 2014}} ==College career== York played limited minutes his freshman season at Arizona and only appeared in 15 games while backing up future [[NBA]] player [[Nick Johnson (basketball)|Nick Johnson]]. During his sophomore season, York saw his playing time increase as he appeared in all 38 games and helped the Wildcats reach their second [[2014–15 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Elite Eight]] appearance.{{cite web|last1=Amacher|first1=Ezra|title=2013–14 Season in Review|url=http://pointguardu.com/2013-14-season-in-review/|website=PointguardU.com|publisher=Gopher Media|accessdate=November 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129081507/http://pointguardu.com/2013-14-season-in-review/|archive-date=November 29, 2014|url-status=dead}} His playing time continued to increase || 1.5 || 0.6 || 0.2 || 9.2 {{S-end}} ==Professional career== ===Guerino Vanoli Basket (2016)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], York joined the [[Charlotte Hornets]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Announce 2016 Orlando Pro Summer League Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-announce-2016-orlando-pro-summer-league-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2016|access-date=November 21, 2016}} On July 22, 2016, York signed with [[Guerino Vanoli Basket|Vanoli Cremona]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]].{{cite news|title=Gabe York signs with Vanoli Cremona|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/207207/gabe-york-signs-with-vanoli-cremona.html|website=Sportando.com|date=July 22, 2016|access-date=July 22, 2016}} On November 15, 2016, he parted ways with Cremona after averaging 4.3 points and 2.5 rebounds in 6 games.{{cite news|title=Gabe York, Vanoli Cremona part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/217458/gabe-york-vanoli-cremona-part-ways.html|work=Sportando.com|date=November 15, 2016|access-date=November 15, 2016}} ===Erie BayHawks (2016–2017)=== Six days after leaving [[Guerino Vanoli Basket|Vanoli Cremona]], he was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|first=Iris|last=Rayburn|title=BayHawks Acquire Gabe York|url=http://erie.dleague.nba.com/news/bayhawks-acquire-gabe-york/|website=NBA.com|date=November 21, 2016|access-date=November 21, 2016}} On December 15, York scored 38 points, two rebounds, four assists and four steals in 38 minutes, including 10 triples in a 118–99 Erie win over the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].{{cite web|title=York's 10 Threes Fuels BayHawks Past D-Fenders|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20161215/LADERI/|website=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2016|accessdate=December 15, 2016}} ===Medi Bayreuth (2017–2018)=== York joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]]. On July 31, 2017, York signed with German club [[Medi Bayreuth]].{{cite news|title=Medi Bayreuth inks Gabe York|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/243000/medi-bayreuth-inks-gabe-york.html|website=Sportando.com|date=July 31, 2017|access-date=July 31, 2017}} Appearing in 37 games (with 37 starts) of the 2017–18 Basketball Bundesliga season, York averaged a team-high 14.2 points per contest, hitting 93 of his 258 three-pointers.{{cite web|title=easyCredit – 425 BAY|url=https://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/easycredit-bbl/historie/teams/t/2017-2018/425-bay/#specialnavi=41|website=EasyCredit-BBL.de|access-date=September 6, 2018|language=German}} ===Lakeland Magic (2018–2019)=== On September 5, 2018, York signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite tweet|author=Orlando Magic PR|number=1037430559335698435|title=RELEASE: Magic sign free agent guard Gabe York|user=Magic_PR|date=September 5, 2018|access-date=September 5, 2018}} On September 27, 2018, York was waived by the Magic.{{cite web|title=Magic Sign Devin Davis Orlando waives Gabe York|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-devin-davis-20180927|website=NBA.com|accessdate=September 27, 2018|date=September 27, 2018}} On October 23, 2018, York was included in the training camp roster of the [[Lakeland Magic]].{{cite web|title=LAKELAND MAGIC FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP 2018}} ===AEK Athens (2019)=== On April 12, 2019, York signed a contract with the [[Greek Basket League]] club [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]], which kept him at the club until the end of the [[2018-19 Greek [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]]{{cite web|title=Mad Ants Announce 2022 Training Camp
